types.name: VisualScriptAsyncEvent
types.doc:
One exec-pin fire from an async action. `pin` indexes the node's exec-output
list (execList). `outputs` are packed onto the node's data-out for this fire.
A terminal fire ends the action and resumes the graph past the node; a
non-terminal (progress) fire runs the pin's chain and keeps the action alive.

Base class for an in-flight async action. Start() runs once with the resolved
node inputs; Tick() runs each frame and pushes any fired events. Return true
while still active, false to retire (a terminal event also retires it).

types.doc:
Asset-load provider for the AsyncLoadAsset action. Visual Scripting sits far below the
asset system, so the node owns only the latent plumbing: the module that
wires the asset manager installs one of these and the node polls it on the
game thread. With none installed the node fires OnFailed on its first tick,
which is the honest answer for a host that has no asset system at all.

types.name: VisualScriptEventGraph
types.doc: One named event graph (e.g. event "BeginPlay" → the graph to run).

types.name: VisualScriptVariable
types.doc:
A class member variable — per-instance state the graphs read/write through
GetVar/SetVar nodes (the Visual Script analog of a Blueprint variable). `type` picks
the VisualScriptValue storage; `defaultValue` seeds it when an instance is created.

members.name: replicated
members.doc:
Replicated (the Visual Script analog of UE's Replicated property specifier). The
authority ships this variable's value to every client whenever it
changes; a remote instance's own write is refused by the VM, the same
way an unroutable RPC is dropped. Container and Custom types are refused
— they have no wire form (see FVisualScriptVarSync).

members.name: repNotify
members.doc:
RepNotify (UE's ReplicatedUsing). Names a custom function of this class
that a RECEIVER runs after an authority update actually changed this
variable's value — the hook a client uses to react to the change (play
the hit flash, refresh the widget) without polling it from Tick. Empty
means no hook; meaningless while `replicated` is off. The function must
take no parameters: the new value is already in the variable when it
runs, and an old-value parameter would need a second copy of every
replicated variable kept per instance for the one hook that reads it.

members.name: instanceEditable
members.doc:
Instance Editable (UE's EditAnywhere on a Blueprint variable). The class
default seeds every instance either way; this decides whether a PLACED
instance may override it from the details panel. Off means the variable
is class-internal state — an inspector row for it would invite a designer
to tune something the graphs treat as private bookkeeping.

members.name: exposeOnSpawn
members.doc:
Expose on Spawn (UE's ExposeOnSpawn). The variable becomes an input pin
on the node that spawns this class, and the value is written onto the
fresh instance BEFORE BeginPlay runs — which is the whole point: a
variable set by a Set node after the spawn returns is already too late
for the spawned actor's own BeginPlay to read.

types.name: VisualScriptFunctionParam
types.doc:
A custom function — a named, callable sub-graph with typed parameters and an
optional return (the Visual Script analog of a Blueprint function). A CallGraphFunction
node invokes it by name; GetParam nodes read its arguments; a Return node sets
the result. Parameters are call-local (a fresh scope per call).

members.name: locals
members.doc:
Call-local variables — seeded from their defaults on every call and
discarded when it returns (GetLocal / SetLocal nodes reach them).

members.name: rpcFlags
members.doc:
FMFunctionFlags::Server / Client / Multicast (+ Reliable): a flagged
function is an RPC with the same routing as a reflected MFUNCTION —
a Call Function of it on the wrong side ships instead of running, and
the receiver re-checks the direction against the packet's origin.
Zero = an ordinary function. An RPC must be void and impure.

types.name: VisualScriptDispatcher
types.doc:
An event dispatcher — a multicast delegate. A Broadcast node fires every
bound handler (a custom function by name), passing the broadcast arguments as
the handler's parameters. The Visual Script analog of a Blueprint Event Dispatcher.

members.name: handlers

types.name: VisualScriptMacroPin
types.doc:
A macro boundary pin — one entry on a macro's input or output side. An exec
pin is a flow tunnel; a data pin carries a typed value. The macro instance
node mirrors these onto its own pins, and expansion inlines the macro's body
in their place.

members.name: type
members.doc: data pins only

types.name: VisualScriptMacro
types.doc:
A macro — a reusable subgraph with N named exec/data inputs and outputs,
INLINED at compile time (the VM never sees a MacroInstance). The Visual Script analog
of a Blueprint macro. The body graph's entry is a MacroInput node (its exec
outputs = the macro's exec inputs, data outputs = data inputs) and it ends at
a MacroOutput node (reached-at-pin j = exec output j; its inputs = data
outputs).

types.name: VisualScriptComponentSlot
types.doc:
A named component slot — the class-description form of "this actor
carries component X with these defaults". Slots apply to the backing ECS
entity at OnConstruct; a child class (or later an instance) redeclaring a
slot with the same name overrides the parent's type/defaults.

that declares neither keeps landing directly on the actor's entity, which
is how every pre-placement .vscript still loads.

members.name: ActorFactory
members.doc:
The gameplay layer's backing-actor factory (returns `new AVisualScriptActor()`
typed as MObject*). Every synthetic class uses it as its MClass.construct.
`nativeBaseClass` names the class the factory actually constructs: a
synthetic declaring a native parent OUTSIDE that class's ancestry would
make IsChildOf lie about an object that is not that type, and every
static_cast through the claim corrupts — registration checks against it.

members.signature: void AddBackingClass(FName nativeParent, ActorFactory factory, FName backingClass)
members.doc:
A backing class for Visual Script classes whose native parent is `nativeParent`
or derives from it: AVisualScriptCharacter for ACharacter, AVisualScriptPawn for APawn.
Registration picks the one nearest the declared parent up its native
chain, and falls back to the SetActorFactory default; before this every
Visual Script class was an AVisualScriptActor whatever it declared.

members.name: Register
members.doc:
Take ownership of `def`, synthesize its MClass, and register it by name.
Returns the synthetic MClass* (also discoverable via MClassRegistry::
FindByName), or nullptr if no factory is installed or the name is taken.

members.name: OrderParentsFirst
members.doc:
Orders parsed classes so every Visual Script parent precedes its children.
Register resolves a class's Visual Script parent once, at registration, and a
parent it cannot find yet reads as native — a child registered first
runs without the parent's variables and graphs for the whole session.
Order is otherwise kept; classes in a parent cycle, or whose parent is
not in the set and not registered, follow in their original order.

members.name: LoadClassFiles
members.signature: static std::vector<std::unique_ptr<VisualScriptClass>> LoadClassFiles(const std::vector<std::string>& paths, std::vector<std::string>* outFailures = nullptr)
members.doc:
Parses every file once, on up to eight workers, and returns the classes
that loaded with a name, in `paths` order (what OrderParentsFirst
takes). A parse touches no registry, so only the registration after it
has to stay on the calling thread; the editor parsed every project
class serially before its first frame. A file that fails is logged and
named in `outFailures`.

members.name: Reregister
members.doc:
Hot-reload: swap the definition behind an already-registered
name. The synthetic MClass instance is REUSED (its pointer is what
live actors and MClassRegistry hold) — only userData / super link
change; children's parentVisualScript links re-point at the new definition.
Falls back to Register when the name is new. Live actors rebind
lazily on their next graph dispatch, keeping variable state.

members.name: Unregister
members.doc:
Drop a registered class (removes it from MClassRegistry and frees its
storage). Returns true if found.

members.name: Revision

members.name: Clear

members.name: AddPending
members.signature: void AddPending(const std::string& className, const std::string& parentClassName, const std::string& path, std::unique_ptr<VisualScriptClass> parsed = nullptr)
members.doc:
Lazy registration. A class known by name and file (FVisualScriptClassIndex)
but not registered: the first FindByName for it — a scene placing one,
a spawn by class — parses (unless `parsed` already holds the definition)
and registers it, parents first; anything enumerating classes
(MClassRegistry::GetAllClasses, CollectClasses) registers every pending
one first. Registering a name directly drops its pending entry. The
first call installs the MClassRegistry hooks.

free.name: kVisualScriptSchemaVersion
free.doc:
Bumped when the on-disk graph schema gains a field. Loaders accept anything
<= this; missing fields fall back to their defaults, so an older .vscript always
reads. v1 = original; v2 = object refs, macros, multi-exec-in pins;
v3 = multi-track Timeline tracks/keys + async-action nodes;
v4 = persisted node canvas positions + comment extents;
v5 = authority nodes (HasAuthority / SwitchHasAuthority) — an older build
maps the unknown kind strings to CallFunction, so the Newer warning is
the only thing standing between such a graph and silent misbehavior;
v6 = replicated class variables + component-slot placement (transform and
attach parent) + the ClassRef node. An older build drops the first two
silently — the class still loads and runs, it just stops replicating and
puts every slot back on the actor's own entity — and maps the unknown
ClassRef kind onto CallFunction, which is why the Newer warning matters;
v7 = per-variable Instance Editable and Expose on Spawn. An older build drops
both silently: instance-editable degrades to "no inspector row", which is
cosmetic, but expose-on-spawn does not — the spawn node keeps the extra
input pins the author wired and the old VM refuses the call on arity, so
the spawn stops happening rather than happening with default values;
v8 = per-variable RepNotify function name. An older build drops it silently
and the variable keeps replicating with no hook — the client state still
converges, only the reaction to it goes missing, so the Newer warning is
advisory rather than load-bearing here;
v9 = the MakeText node and its ns/key/src properties. An older build maps the
unknown kind onto CallFunction, so the node stops producing a string at
all — a label goes blank rather than going untranslated, which is why
the Newer warning matters again here.

types.name: FVisualScriptSpawnScope
types.doc:
The exposed values of one spawn, armed for the duration of the spawn call on
the calling thread. The gameplay layer's spawn path consumes them at the one
moment that works — after the fresh instance has its class bound (which seeds
every variable with the class default and would otherwise overwrite them) and
before it is registered (which runs OnConstruct and, in a world already
playing, BeginPlay).

Scopes nest by construction order because a spawned actor's BeginPlay may
spawn again; the inner scope hides the outer one and restores it on the way
out. A consumed scope stays armed but refuses a second take, so a re-entrant
spawn can never inherit the values of the one it ran inside.

verb gets the pins with no engine change.

The name is part of the rule because reflection carries no parameter
names (MowoHeaderTool emits types only) and because signature shape alone
cannot tell a spawn from a lookup: MActorStatics::GetActorOfClassAt is

types.name: EVisualScriptNetMode
types.doc:
Network role of a graph run. Standalone (the default) is "no session": every
RPC-flagged call executes locally, UE-style. Authority is the server/host (or
a client-local actor that was never replicated — it is its own authority);
Remote is a replicated actor's client-side instance.

types.name: EVisualScriptRpcRoute
types.doc:
What the routeRpc hook did with a call it was handed. Sent = the call left
on the wire and must NOT run locally; RunLocal = the resolved destination is
this machine (e.g. a Client RPC whose owning client is the listen host), so
the VM invokes it locally after all; Failed = it could not be routed (target
not replicated, marshalling refused) — the call is DROPPED with an error,
never executed on the wrong machine.

types.name: FVisualScriptSlotCache
types.doc:
One instance's resolution of graph nodes to entries in its variable store:
by node index, the GetVar / SetVar / container-mutator variable, latch state
or Timeline state the node reads and writes, null until the node first runs.
A name-keyed store costs a string hash and probe per node per run, and an
unnamed latch also built its key string on every hit; resolved once, a node
reaches its entry through one pointer. The entries point into the
unordered_map that `VisualScriptContext::vars` names, which keeps element addresses
across insertion and rehash, so the owner must Clear() whenever it erases,
clears, moves or reassigns that map, or when the graphs it was resolved
against may have been freed (a definition hot swap).

members.name: Clear
members.doc: Drops every row. Only between runs: a run in progress holds its row.

members.name: Invalidate
members.doc:
Forgets every resolution but keeps the rows, so it is safe while a run
on this instance is in progress (a nested run can reach it).

types.name: FVisualScriptFrame
types.doc:
One call's parameters and locals, laid out by slot: the values in one
vector, the names pointing at the function's own declarations. A call used
to build an unordered_map — a node allocation and a string copy per local
and parameter, a hash and a probe per GetParam / GetLocal / SetLocal. A
node resolves its slot once per call (ForNode); the debugger, the DAP and a
host that seeds a call scope by name still reach it by name.

members.name: Bind
members.signature: void Bind(const VisualScriptFunction& fn, const std::vector<VisualScriptValue>& args)
members.doc:
Locals at their declared defaults, then the parameters from `args` (a
missing argument is a default value). A parameter named like a local
takes that local's slot, which is what the map it replaced did.

members.name: Reset
members.doc:
Empties the frame and releases what its values hold, keeping the
vectors' capacity for the next Bind (the per-thread frame pool).

members.name: Find
members.signature: const VisualScriptValue* Find(const std::string& name) const

members.name: FindOrAdd
members.doc:
A name with no declaration gets a slot of its own (SetLocal of an
undeclared name, a debugger write).

members.signature: VisualScriptValue* ForNode(const VisualScriptGraph* graph, int nodeIdx, size_t nodeCount, const std::string& name)
members.doc:
`nodeIdx` of `graph` resolved to its slot on first use and by index
after; a different graph (a debugger expression run in this frame)
starts a fresh resolution. Null when the name is not in the frame.

members.name: ForEach
members.signature: template<typename Fn> void ForEach(Fn&& fn) const

types.name: VisualScriptContext
types.doc:
Execution context for a graph run: the call target + its class (for
call-by-reflection), an optional per-instance variable store that
GetVar/SetVar nodes read and write, and (for custom functions) the VisualScriptClass
whose function sub-graphs CallGraphFunction can invoke. The variable store is
owned by the caller (e.g. AVisualScriptActor) so values persist across event graphs.

members.name: slotCache
members.doc:
The owner's node-to-entry resolution for `vars`; null runs every lookup
by name. Never set it for a transient graph (a debugger expression): its
address can be reused by the next one.

members.name: visualScriptClass
members.doc: resolves CallGraphFunction by name

members.name: graphKey
members.doc:
Identity of the graph being run ("BeginPlay", a function name, …). Latch
state (DoOnce / FlipFlop / Gate / DoN / MultiGate) with no author-given
name is keyed by NODE INDEX, which is graph-local: without this salt a
DoOnce at index 3 in BeginPlay and one at index 3 in Tick shared a latch,
so the second never fired. Named latches deliberately ignore it — a Gate
and the SetGate that opens it are meant to address one state by name
across graphs. The pointer must outlive the run (an event name off the
VisualScriptClass, or a literal); null falls back to the pre-salt keys.

members.name: params
members.doc: Call-local scope (set only while running a function sub-graph):

members.name: currentFunction
members.doc: entry-node param pins resolve through this

members.name: returnSlot
members.doc: Return writes here

members.name: depth
members.doc: recursion guard

members.name: allowLatent
members.doc:
When true, a Delay node SUSPENDS the run (event graphs). When false it
runs instantly (inside custom functions — no cross-function suspension).

members.name: void
members.signature: void (*firePin)(void* user, const std::string& pin, const VisualScriptValue& payload) = nullptr
members.doc:
Pin routing hook. A FirePin node calls this with the pin name and
an optional payload; the gameplay layer (AVisualScriptActor → MWorld wire table)
routes it to every connected instance's input pin. Null = pins inert.

members.name: netMode
members.doc:
Network role of this run — drives HasAuthority/SwitchHasAuthority and
decides whether an RPC-flagged CallFunction/CallOn executes locally or
routes through the hook below.

members.name: EVisualScriptRpcRoute
members.signature: EVisualScriptRpcRoute (*routeRpc)(void* user, MObject* target, const FMFunctionInfo& fn, const VisualScriptValue* args, size_t argCount) = nullptr
members.doc:
RPC routing hook. When a graph calls an RPC-flagged MFUNCTION that must
run on ANOTHER machine (Server flag on a client, Client/Multicast flag on
the authority), the VM hands the resolved call here instead of invoking
the thunk; the gameplay layer (AVisualScriptActor → FNetSession) marshals the
args and ships it. `args` are already coerced to the parameter types.
Null hook while netMode != Standalone = such calls are dropped with an
error — they never execute on the wrong machine.

members.name: bool
members.signature: bool (*callVisualScriptFunctionOn)(void* user, MObject* target, const std::string& functionName, const std::vector<VisualScriptValue>& args, VisualScriptValue* ret) = nullptr
members.doc:
visual-script-function call on ANOTHER Visual Script object. Call On Target resolves a
reflected MFUNCTION first; when the target's synthetic class declares a
Visual Script function of that name instead, the VM hands the call here and the
gameplay layer runs it against the TARGET's variable store, which only
it owns. Returns true when the function ran; `ret` takes its return.
Null hook = Visual Script functions are reachable on self only.

types.name: VisualScriptDebugHook
types.doc:
Debugger hook — the runtime half of the Visual Script DAP. When installed,
the VM calls onNode before dispatching every exec node (breakpoint check /
single-step); returning false ABORTS the run (debugger stop). ctx.vars are
live for inspection. Process-global — one debugger per process.

members.signature: bool (*onNode)(void* user, const VisualScriptGraph& g, int nodeIdx, const VisualScriptContext& ctx) = nullptr

types.name: VisualScriptExecItem
types.doc:
One item on the VM's explicit exec stack. Capturing execution in data (rather
than the C++ call stack) is what lets a Delay suspend and resume the graph.

members.name: node
members.doc: node to run, or the control node (Sequence/ForLoop/While)

members.name: index
members.doc: SeqResume: next output; LoopIter: current iteration

members.name: after
members.doc: LoopIter: the "completed" exec target

types.name: VisualScriptContinuation
types.doc:
A suspended graph run — saved when a Delay or Timeline fires. Holds the
remaining exec stack + the node outputs computed so far (so data links across
the wait still resolve). `graph` must stay alive (event graphs live in the
VisualScriptClass).

members.name: graphKey
members.doc:
The suspended run's graph identity, restored into the context on resume
so a latch downstream of a Delay keys the same slot it would have without
the wait. Points into the VisualScriptClass, whose latents are purged whenever
the definition is swapped.

members.name: stack
members.doc: resume target after the wait/finish

members.name: remaining
members.doc: Delay: seconds until resume

members.name: active
members.doc: true while this holds a real suspension

members.name: timelineNode
members.doc: Timeline only:

members.name: updateExec
members.doc: exec pulsed each frame

members.name: timelineMulti
members.doc: multi-track timeline (state lives in ctx.vars)

members.name: async
members.doc:
Async only: the in-flight action ticked each frame; its exec-output pins
resume the graph when they fire.

members.name: Execute
members.signature: static bool Execute(const VisualScriptGraph& graph, const VisualScriptContext& ctx, VisualScriptContinuation* outCont = nullptr)
members.doc:
Run `graph` in `ctx`. Returns true if it ran without error. If a Delay
suspends the run AND `outCont` is non-null, *outCont is filled with the
continuation (active=true) for the caller to schedule; pass ctx.allowLatent
= true to enable that. Without a sink, Delays run instantly.

members.name: Execute
members.signature: static bool Execute(const VisualScriptGraph& graph, MObject* target, MClass* cls)
members.doc: Convenience: no variable store, no latent.

members.signature: static bool CallGraphFunctionByName(const VisualScriptClass& cls, const std::string& functionName, const VisualScriptContext& ctx, const std::vector<VisualScriptValue>& args, VisualScriptValue& outReturn)

members.name: Resume
members.signature: static bool Resume(VisualScriptContinuation& cont, const VisualScriptContext& ctx)
members.doc:
Resume a suspended Delay continuation NOW (runs its saved stack). If it
suspends again, `cont` stays active; otherwise cont.active becomes false.

members.name: Advance
members.signature: static bool Advance(VisualScriptContinuation& cont, float dt, const VisualScriptContext& ctx)
members.doc:
Advance a continuation by `dt` seconds (call each frame). Delays resume
when their timer elapses; Timelines pulse their update exec every frame
(alpha 0..1 on the timeline node's data-out) and finish at the end.
Returns true if still active (keep it queued), false when done.

members.name: SetDebugHook
members.doc:
Install/clear the process-wide debug hook. Not thread-safe with
concurrent VM runs — install while the game thread is idle.

members.name: SetRandomSeed
members.doc:
Seed the RandomInt/RandomFloat/MultiGate-random stream for the CALLING
thread (state is thread-local, so runs on other threads keep their own
sequence). Deterministic replays and tests seed before executing; a
seed of 0 restores the default stream.

members.name: RandomBits
members.doc:
The raw xorshift draw behind RandomInt / RandomFloat / MultiGate-random.
Exposed so TRANSPILED classes draw from the same seeded per-thread stream
the VM does — a native body with its own generator would diverge from the
interpreted one the moment a test seeded it.

members.name: PooledFrameCapacity
members.doc:
Node-output slots held by the calling thread's reusable run frames. A
run borrows the frame for its nesting depth and hands it back emptied,
so this stops growing once the deepest graph has run once.

members.name: ResolveCacheMisses
members.doc:
Name resolutions (reflected function or property by name) the calling
thread did NOT find in its cache. A graph calling the same function a
thousand times resolves it once, until a class registers, unregisters
or a Visual Script class is rebuilt.

members.name: DataPinCopies
members.doc:
Data-pin reads on the calling thread that copied a value out of where
it lives (a variable, a parameter, a stored output). Node evaluation
reads those in place; what is left here is the by-value API at the
edges (call arguments, setters, the debugger).

types.name: VisualScriptContainer
types.doc:
Container shape of a pin. `type` keeps describing the ELEMENT type, so an
array of ints is { type = Int, container = Array } — the pin colouring and
the reflected-call marshalling both keep working off `type` alone.

types.name: VisualScriptObjRef
types.doc:
How an Object CONSTANT resolves to a live actor. A hard pointer can never
persist (the object doesn't exist at load time), so a serialized object pin
carries a symbolic reference resolved against the world when the graph runs.

members.name: None
members.doc: not a reference (raw / runtime-produced object value)

members.name: Self
members.doc: the graph's execution target

members.name: Name
members.doc: an actor found by its object name (`str`)

members.name: Tag
members.doc: the first actor carrying tag (`str`)

types.name: FVisualScriptStructBox
types.doc:
A struct value known only by name (FTransform, any copyable MSTRUCT): an
owned, constructed instance, deep-copied with the value. It is what lets a
Custom pin hand a thunk a pointer to exactly the C++ type it casts to.

types.name: FVisualScriptHeapRef
types.doc:
The owning handle of a value's out-of-line part. Copies SHARE the block and
the first mutable access through a shared handle clones it, so copying a
string or container value — every pin read, variable read and argument —
is a reference-count bump, not a deep copy, while a write never reaches
another value's data.

types.name: FVisualScriptObjectSlot
types.doc:
An object pin's live handle. It shares the scalar slot: an object value
never carries a number.

members.name: ptr
members.doc: marshalling cache (MObject* resolved from `weak`), or a legacy raw pointer

types.name: VisualScriptValue
types.doc:
32 bytes on a 64-bit build: the tags, one 16-byte slot shared by every
scalar, the quaternion and the object handle, and one pointer to the
copy-on-write block holding strings, containers and struct instances. It
used to carry all of those side by side (~240 bytes, then ~150), and pin
outputs, variables and call arguments are copied by value on every
evaluation.

Only the slot member `type` names is meaningful. Writing one member and
reading another reinterprets bytes, so a value must never carry two scalar
facts at once (pack them into one member, as the Timeline state packs into
v4) and cross-type readers go through the typed accessors below.

members.name: type
members.doc:
The one-byte tags sit together so the struct pays a single padding run
for all of them.

members.name: keyType
members.doc: Map only

members.name: objRef
members.doc: Object CONSTANT: how it resolves

members.name: objWeak
members.doc:
Object pins hold a WEAK handle — never a hard pointer and never a GC
root, so a graph can outlive its referent safely. `objWeak` distinguishes
a live object value (resolve through `object.weak`) from a legacy raw
pointer.

members.name: assetRef
members.doc:
A String CONSTANT that names an asset: the graph serializer writes it as
a typed reference so the cook, delete-safety and map check see it, and
reading a typed value back sets it again. Runtime values ignore it.

members.name: Str
members.doc:
Strings, container elements, map keys and struct instances live in the
shared block. The const views never allocate (an absent block reads
empty); the Mutable ones create the block, or clone it when another value
still shares it.

members.name: Items
members.doc: Array elements / Map values / Set elements

members.name: Keys
members.doc: Map keys (parallel to Items)

members.name: Struct
members.doc: Custom: the struct instance and its ops

members.name: AsVec2
members.doc: The typed view of the shared slot, zero when `type` is something else.

members.name: AsQuat
members.doc:
A zero quaternion is not a rotation; it is what an unwritten Quat slot
holds, and it has always meant the identity.

members.name: MakeStruct
members.doc:
A default-constructed struct of the named type, or an empty Custom
value (no storage — a call taking it is refused) when the type is not
registered.

members.name: FromObject
members.doc:
A live object pin from an MObject — captures a weak handle (the only
GC-safe way to hold an object in a graph value).

members.name: MakeObjectRef
members.signature: static VisualScriptValue MakeObjectRef(VisualScriptObjRef kind, const std::string& ref)
members.doc:
A serialized object reference (Self / find-by-name / find-by-tag),
resolved against the live world when the graph runs.

members.name: ResolveObject
members.doc:
The live MObject behind an object pin, or nullptr when empty / collected
/ not an object at all — the handle shares the scalar slot, so another
type's bytes must never be read as a pointer. Weak-checked, so a swept
referent reads back as null (never a dangle).

members.name: HasLiveWeakObject
members.doc:
A weak object handle that still resolves — what a constant object pin
dropped in from the world carries.

Structural equality — the comparison behind array Contains/Find and map
key lookup. Numeric types compare by value across int/float.

members.name: Storage

Pointer to the storage matching `type` (for the invoke ABI). Returns
nullptr for Void / unsupported types and for containers (a container
never marshals into a reflected call). A String or Custom value is made
unshared first: the thunk may write through the pointer.

True when `v` has a wire form. Containers, Object and Custom are out:
a container has no fixed payload, and an object reference would need the
replication address book, which is what makes it a component's job.

Pack name/value pairs. Entries with no wire form are SKIPPED with a
warning rather than failing the whole update — one bad variable must not
stop the rest of an actor's state from converging.
